identity_notes: Genuine oral free-L-histidine human supplementation evidence in this retrieved scope is extremely sparse: only 6 of 160 records concern actual histidine intake in humans, and even among those, several abstracts were truncated before reporting quantitative results in this retrieval. The single most important applicability caveat: the overwhelming majority of 'histidine' records (roughly half of the full 160) concern histidine-tryptophan-ketoglutarate (HTK/Custodiol) solution, an entirely different use case — a buffered organ-preservation and cardioplegia perfusate used ex vivo/intraoperatively in transplant surgery and cardiac surgery, with no relevance to oral dietary supplementation. A second large cluster (~40 records) is generic metabolomics/biomarker-discovery literature (cancer, cardiovascular, metabolic disease) in which histidine appears only as one of dozens of measured plasma/serum/urine metabolites, not as an administered intervention. A third cluster concerns carnosine, anserine, and beta-alanine (histidine-containing dipeptides or its precursor) which are distinct supplements covered under the separate l_carnosine identity and were excluded here as different_substance. The oldest genuine trial (PMID 342692, rheumatoid arthritis, 4.5 g/day x 30 weeks) found no clinical benefit over placebo.
